transcriptSegments.text: Hello, Stanley House Courses. Oh, hello.
I'm ringing to book a place on one of your weekend courses. Very good.
Which course are you interested in? Well, a guitar one.
I think it was a workshop, actually. That's right.
And when did you want to come?
Well, I was thinking of the weekend of July the 16th, if there's room then.
Let me just check.
Oh, the 16th is a Wednesday. Did you mean the 18th? Oh, sorry.
Yes, I was looking at the wrong month. No problem. Yes, you're in luck.
There are three places left there, so I'll put you down for one.
So the code for that is Q1632.
That's just for our reference.
So now for a few details.
Can I just check if you've done any of our weekend courses before?
Yes, in fact, I have.
I did one last September. It was on photographs.
We learnt about editing them. I really enjoyed it.
Yes, that's always a popular course.
So your details will be on the computer already. Let me see.
I can just have your name, please. It's Nick Poskitt.
Oh, that's an unusual name, isn't it? Right, here we are.
So is your address still 27 Hawthorne Road?
Oh, it's Hawthorne Way, actually.
OK, I'll correct that now.
And it's Bristol BS42QG?
That's right. Lovely.
And the next thing I need from you is a contact phone number.
Thanks.
That's just in case we need to get hold of you in an emergency.
Now, if you've stayed with us before, you'll know that our guests all stay in shared accommodation.
And we've had quite a lot of requests lately for people to be put in with someone of a similar age.
So can I ask how old you are? Sure, I'm 26.
And can I ask your occupation? Engineer.
I wish I could say musician, but maybe one day. Let's hope so.
OK, so now about meals.
Do you have any special dietary requirements?
Well, I don't like any sort of fish.
I'm fine with everything else. That's fine.
I'll make a note of that.
OK, and if I could ask you just one more question about the course, Nick? Sure.
On the Saturday afternoon, you can choose to have an individual one-to-one lesson on one particular aspect of guitar playing.
So you can choose jazz guitar? Hmm, probably not. Yes, maybe. Or rock?
That sounds good, but no, I think I'll go for the second one. OK, fine.
I didn't know we had individual classes.
It didn't mention that in the information I read about the course.
Where did you actually find out about us?
Well, this time I just looked on your website, but I originally found out about you from a magazine.
Right, yes, we'll have to update the website, but our prices are up to date. So it's still £370?
That's right.
Before I take your card details, is there anything else I can help you with?
Well, last time I came I travelled by train and someone met me at the station, but this time I'll be driving.
So will there be parking available? I'll see what I can do.
I can't promise it, but I'll do my best.
It's a good thing you mentioned it, actually, as places are limited. Great.
Right, so if there's nothing else, I'll just take your credit card number. OK, it's 78956.
I'd like to welcome Sam Goodwin to the programme.
He's one of the organisers of this year's Denford Festival.
So, Sam, what can you tell us about what's happening this year?
Well, as usual, the festival will take place during the first weekend in August, and there will be things going on all over the town.
There are a number of separate areas, each with their own special attraction and atmosphere.
Let's start with Bridge Street.
Local schoolchildren took part in a competition to paint pictures of the local landscape, and you'll be able to see all their work displayed here.
The winning entries have also been made into postcards that you can buy at one of the stalls.
At Kings Park, we've built a climbing wall, and there'll also be an inflatable bouncy castle for kids to burn off excess energy.
Both are going to be supervised by volunteer teachers at all times, so parents can go off and enjoy other parts of the festival.
There's a lot happening in Oakvale School.
If you're over 18, there's an exciting contest to take part in here.
You'll have an hour to prepare your favourite food or dish, and the prizes will be presented by our special guest, the singer Maria Thompson.
On Green Road, we'll have some top local groups performing
and singing throughout the day until 5, including the Denford Choir, who've just come back from a really successful tour of Australia and New Zealand.
And finally, I'll mention Sun Lane.
We want you to leave the festival with more than good memories, and a full stomach, so we'd encourage everyone to go to Sun Lane,
where we'll have a number of experts giving tips and advice on how to successfully grow your own fruit and vegetables.
You never know, maybe next year we'll be showing your produce.
Thank
you, Sam.
That all sounds really interesting.
And you've got some practical information for us.
Yes, this year's festival will be bigger than ever, judging by ticket sales so far.
Tickets can be purchased from our website or at the festival on the day, although those will cost a bit more.
The tickets give you free entry to most areas, although you do need to pay extra to get into some of the special events.
We're doing something different this year on the final evening of the festival.
We usually have a big firework display, but it's proven too expensive this year.
So instead, we're holding a dance for everyone who wants to come.
That's going to be in the local theatre, where we'll clear away all the chairs to give us plenty of room.
It should be great fun.
We're expecting a large number of international visitors, so you'll be hearing a lot of different languages around the festival this year.
And we've organised a help desk to advise people on finding accommodation if they need it.
We'll also be offering day trips to points of interest in the region at very reasonable prices.
If you do decide to drive, there are two festival car parks.
Car Park A to the north and Car Park B in the east.
Car Park B is in the middle of town, so it usually fills up very quickly.
From Car Park A, there is a 15-minute walk along the river to the town centre.
It takes a little longer to get to the festival, but it's twice the size of B, and it's a nice flat walk.
There's one more change I'd like to tell you about.
Last year, we sent out nearly 30,000 free programmes with the tickets, and we're aware of both the cost and the environmental impact of this.
We looked into having an app instead, but that was too expensive.
So, in the end, we decided to put the programme on our website and save that way.
You'll still be able to pick up a hard copy at the festival if you want.
Dr. Williams. Come in. Thanks. How can I help you?
Well, I'm interested in doing the course on action research. Sure. What would you like to know?
Well, first of all, I understand it's about ways of researching your own practise in your professional role so as to improve it.
That's right, and I'm afraid I must emphasise at the outset that it's only open to working teachers.
Well, I've been one for eight years, so... That's plenty, and... And can I ask, will you be teaching out?
Yes, I've done so for many years, but the course leader will be one of our new lecturers, Alan Cumner. Oh.
He's just written a very interesting book on action research, which you should get hold of.
The title is Professional Learning. Right.
I think one of the other teachers in my school mentioned it. Okay.
Can I ask you what will be covered on the course?
Well, the obvious aim is to develop skills in using a variety of research techniques. Yes, of course.
I'll ask you about those in more detail later.
And then there's something that's crucial to action research, and that's the skill of researching in a team. Yes.
I can say that it is very important.
And what about after you've done the research?
